questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: The opportunity for a personal and social experience and to live abroad for a while.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Smaller city, close to nature, far away from Denmark, English speaking country, "The American University Experience"

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My overall study abroad experience was severely (negatively) affected by personal matters at home.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy and my host university also provided very quick email responses to my questions. The first week was quiet as most of the students who were going to live in residence has not yet arrived.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
The International Centre for Students provided tons of introduction and social activities the first week before school started. 
Residence Service provided the information and help neccesary for move-in etc.
After the first week community leaders in residence also provided help and information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: However it was also a bit overwhelming and I had to choose between acties as attending all would have been too much.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Cluster housing, Pod style rooms (with shared kitchen, bath and washrooms) and Standard rooms (single and double).

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Meal plans were mandatory for standard rooms and optional for the rest as kitchen facilities were available for cluster and pod style.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
It is quite difficult to get a spot because they have first-year guarantee and a lottery. I think I only got my room because I applied for Priority Consideration. It is also not possible to have your own shower, toilet and kitchen. 
However it was very nice living on campus and I definetly recommend it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Victoria is a difficult and expensive place to find housing in. I was super lucky!

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I thought that spots were going to fill up quickly but I was positively surprised that they did not. If you have to apply for prerequisites, be sure that the system has coded your information before course registration start. Also be sure to registrate at your designated time spot.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
- I spend MANY hours reading about the different courses in the course calender
- I made a list of 10-15 possible courses
- I applied for prerequisites
- I prioritized and made a time scheduele in their registration platform
- I registrered at my designated time and got all of my course wishes

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A thourough email guide, video tutorial, material on the webpage, Zoom meeting and help through phone or email.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be ready to spend a lot of time choosing your courses and preparing for the actual registration.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I enjoyed taking courses a bit outside my primary study area in Denmark. Courses are organized quite differently with less class time and a little less reading but much more additional work such as quizzes, assignments, reports etc.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had 100, 200 and 300 level courses corresponding to the first 3 years of a bachelor/undergraduate (in Canada a bachelor degree is 4 years). I found the courses to be a step below the level of my Danish courses. However based on the University system's differences you will not only meet first year students in 100-level classes, it is a lot more mixed and it is normal to take some courses quite different from you primary study area.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Classes and lectures were similar but some were expecting a bit more interaction and participation from student (this was in some courses also part of your final grade). Your grade does not only rely on the final exam as in Denmark which I both liked and disliked. It took a lot of pressure of the final exam but gave you no chance to fall a little behind on reading etc. As mentioned above they also put a lot of more focus on assignments, quizzes etc.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduction to Anthropology
Primate Behavioural Ecology
The Search for Life in the Universe
Introduction to Ceramics - Wheel and Hand Building Techniques

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
All of them! 
But I was a little overwhelmed by the report and assignment workload in The Search for Life in the Universe even though it was a really interesting astronomy course including observatory experience and labs.
Introduction to Anthropology was a great and broad introductory course with a really nice and modern professor and fun and interesting preparation material. 
Primate Behavioural Ecology was my favorite course. Such a great teacher and it had no final exam but instead a poster project that taught me a lot. I also made a Canadian friend in this course.
I also enjoyed Ceramics and recommed it to anyone who likes being creative. However be prepared of a teacher grading hard and to spend a lot of time in the studio outside of class.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Laundry, change of flight tickets, taxi a few times, medication

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was more expensive than expected (especially grocery shopping)! The rest was about what I expected and about the same level as in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: For personal reasons I wasn't able to take part in as many non-academic opportunities as I would have liked. The possibilities however seemed interesting and plentiful.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: First-Nation cultural experiences, lots of sports (including fitness and swimming pool), clubs (I encourage future students to look into this), international student events, residence events, Student Wellness Centre, Multifaith, Vikes etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I encourage future students to look into the clubs because there are so many opportunities and interests covered in them.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Nature and animals (I saw several bears, eagles, seals, otters, orcas, humpback whales etc)! Plan trips around Vancouver Island, take the ferry to Vancouver, Port Angelses (Washington State, USA) or Seattle. Go on lots of hikes and spend some time in downtown Victoria as well. Go to the beach (very close to UVic) and take a bunch of beautiful photos. I also did a road trip in Alberta (Banff and Jasper) before my exchange stay.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. The Canadian people are super friendly and polite. They put a lot of focus on equality for minorities such as indigeneous people or people with handicap. The Canadian accent is not difficult to understand and you will not be the only one who have a foreign accent.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try to engage with the Canadian students in your classes or at clubs/events. Don't be afraid to take initiative, you will most likely be met with a possitive experience but you also have to put yourself out there. People probably won't come to you first but will include you when you have opened up.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None. It was a perfect balance of something similar and something new. The only cultural thing I missed was probably Danish food.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendlyness and willingness to help. That you were always asked if you are okay with this and that. I also really appreciated their views on climate and nature and equal rights for everyone.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Bring your outdoor gear!
- Be prepared to study in a different way than in Denmark (and don't be afraid of the courses being too hard).
- Take advantage of all of the opportunities that UVic provides - from social activities, to counceling, to a diverse array of courses and nature and opportunities for experiences all around. Don't be afraid to try new things and put yourself out there, but also remember that you can't do it all and it is important to take personal breaks as well.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Be aware of the housing situation and know that Canada is NOT a cheap country to live in. 
Ask for all the help you need (also maybe more than you need) - they are very willing to help.
UVic is located on an island and it is not possible to enter or exit the island by other means than ferry or plane.
Remember to apply for eTa (Canada) and ESTA (USA) so it will be easy to go on trips and cross the boader.
Know that it is definetly most easy to get around (outside of the greater Victoria area) by car.
Remember that your grades go back on your Danish transcript as pass/no pass, so invest some of your time outside of the academics.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
My travel experiences. Canada is an amazingly beautiful country!
My English language skills improved as well as my ability to produce reports and assigments in writing.
Trying to be completely on my own with my family being so far away was rewarding in a developing manner.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
Personal circumstances back home which made me isolate and miss out on a lot of social relationships and opportunities for activities. 
I felt very alone and far away from everything and everyone in having to deal with personal matters happening at home during my stay. I considered going home several times but decided to stay.
I ended up being 5 reports behind in one of my courses that I then had to write in the final week. It was probably one of the hardest thing I have ever had to do in such a short time. I had already gotten extensions but I tried reasoning with the professor (without succes) that my personal circumstances should allow me to miss some of them.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer:
Go for it! 
Choose UVic for it's unique location, for it's size (both the city and student body) and for it's many opportunities.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
